gloss: many; much; a large number; mostly

definitions.gloss: many; much; a large number; the majority
definitions.explanation: A large number or amount of something. Functions as a noun, often followed by の (多くの = many) or used with が/は as a subject meaning 'most' or 'the majority.'

definitions.gloss: mostly; for the most part; in many cases
definitions.explanation: Used adverbially to indicate that something is true in the majority of cases.

examples.japanese: {多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{参加|さんか}した。
{学生|がくせい}の{多|おお}くは{通学|つうがく}に{電車|でんしゃ}を{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: Most of the students use the train to commute to school.

examples.japanese: この{地域|ちいき}では{多|おお}くの{場合|ばあい}、{車|くるま}がないと{不便|ふべん}だ。
examples.english: In this area, it's inconvenient without a car in most cases.

examples.japanese: {日本人|にほんじん}は{多|おお}く{語|かた}らない。
examples.english: Japanese people for the most part don't talk a lot.

examples.japanese: {休日|きゅうじつ}は{多|おお}くを{家|いえ}で{過|す}ごす。
examples.english: I spend most of my days off at home.

examples.japanese: {被害|ひがい}を{受|う}けた{建物|たてもの}の{多|おお}くは{築|ちく}30{年以上|ねんいじょう}のものだった。
examples.english: Most of the damaged buildings were over 30 years old.

notes:
The noun/adverb form of {多|おお}い (many). While {多|おお}い exists as an adjective, it cannot directly modify a noun — *{多|おお}い{人|ひと} is ungrammatical. Use {多|おお}くの instead.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {多|おお}くの + noun: many ~ ({多|おお}くの{人|ひと}: many people)
- ~の{多|おお}く: most of ~ ({学生|がくせい}の{多|おお}く: most students)
- {多|おお}くの{場合|ばあい}: in many cases
- {多|おお}くを{語|かた}らない: not to say much

WATCH OUT:
Learners often write {多|おお}い{人|ひと} instead of {多|おお}くの{人|ひと} or {人|ひと}が{多|おお}い. This is one of the most common errors with {多|おお}い.
